journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
title: Enhancement of Hydrogen Storage Capacity of Zeolite-Templated Carbons by Chemical Activation
material_description: ZTC1 | zeolite-templated carbon (template: zeolite Y CBV720, Zeolyst International, Si/Al 15); 0.6 g zeolite, acetonitrile CVD in Ar for 3 h at 800 C, then 900 C for 3 h in Ar; zeolite removed with HF/HCl; Section 2.1 gives 800 C CVD for ZTC1, the Results text says ZTC1 was prepared at 700 C
purification_method: zeolite Y template removed by washing with 10% HF several times, then refluxing in concentrated HCl at 60 C
source_location: main article p. 11317 (page image main-4), Figure 3, series (c) ZTC1, filled red circles
notes: archive: fig3_c_ZTC1.json; Figure 3 series (c) ZTC1, filled red circles; the paper states these isotherms are completely reversible with no hysteresis but does not distinguish adsorption and desorption points in the figure, so some plotted points may be desorption points (coded adsorption); isotherm_point_count = 28 counts only the markers that could be separated (lower bound): markers below about 2.3 bar overlap into one band and were neither digitized nor counted; T printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored 77.15 K; gravimetric Hiden IGA-003 microbalance; buoyancy correction stated (carbon density 1.5 g/cm3 and hydrogen density 0.04 g/cm3 'used for buoyancy correction of adsorbed hydrogen'); uptake basis not named, so uptake_type unspecified and basis_inferred excess by the gravimetric-with-buoyancy-correction default; skeletal_density_g_cm3 holds that assumed carbon density (not measured); packing_density_g_cm3 holds the packing density the paper assumes from refs 22a,32,33 for its volumetric estimate (not measured); degassed at 120 C overnight (duration not numeric) to 10^-7 bar (stored 0.01 Pa); H2 99.9999% further purified by a molecular sieve filter; BET range: 0.06-0.22; total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 ~0.99, micropore surface area and micropore volume by t-plot (pore_volume_method gives the micropore method); DFT (NLDFT, N2) pore size maxima 1.3/2.2 nm not stored as a single diameter
